rationale: When a team unexpectedly loses a player, the market-implied distribution over game margin can translate (a change in expected strength), widen (a change in uncertainty) or fatten at the blowout end (a different failure mode). These are distinct economic claims and only a ladder separates them. Kalshi's KXNFLSPREAD lists P(TEAM margin > strike) for both teams, which composes exactly into a survival curve over signed home margin. The question has never been asked because no one has reconstructed the surface.
features: market-implied margin survival curve from both teams' KXNFLSPREAD rungs at minute resolution, reconstructed at shock-5m, shock, +10m, +30m, +60m and close; shock = kickoff-90m (inactive release, exact by league rule); treatment = the CORRECTED surprise-inactive population
target: three separately reported components of the pre -> +60m change: location (implied median margin), scale (implied interquartile width) and tail (P(|margin| > 13.5)), each differenced against matched no-shock control games over the identical clock offsets
expected_direction: Prior is that a skill-position absence moves location slightly and does not change shape. A scale or tail response significantly larger than the location response would be the interesting outcome, since it would mean the ladder carries information the moneyline cannot express.
test_plan: PREREGISTERED BEFORE 2026 DATA EXISTS. Primary endpoint: 40 treated and 40 control games with a reconstructable pre AND +60m ladder pair. alpha = 0.01 across the three components. Thresholds are fixed in scripts/research/ladder_shock_repricing.py and the script prints NO VERDICT until they are met. The tail is never extrapolated past the widest quoted strike; a stale (>15m) quote is refused rather than carried forward; books wider than 10 cents and ladders under 6 rungs are dropped.
dataset: KXNFLSPREAD minute candles (market-data) + research/shocks/shocks_2025.parquet + 2026 capture stream
result: UNTESTED -- not a null. The 2025 KXNFLSPREAD minute-candle archive covers only 22 games (week 18 and the playoffs); Kalshi did not list spread ladders for the 2025 regular season. 18 games yield a reconstructable pre/+60m pair: 14 treated, 4 control. Four controls cannot support a matched design and the preregistered gate is not met. Descriptives only, all well inside 1 SE of zero on both sides: location treated +0.052+-0.103 vs control -0.146+-0.182; scale +0.088+-0.094 vs -0.064+-0.241; tail -0.0013+-0.0025 vs -0.0050+-0.0029. Incidental observation worth more than the aggregate: 6 of the 14 treated games show an implied median that does not move AT ALL across the full 90 minutes, which is a market with no flow rather than a market absorbing news slowly.
notes: The one part of session 4 that produced no answer, and the reason is data availability rather than a negative result. The machinery is built, tested (tests/test_ladder_shock_repricing.py pins the away-side complement, monotonicity, the staleness rule, no-forward-looking and the no-extrapolation rule) and gated in advance, so 2026 answers the question with thresholds chosen before the data existed.
